details.description: Claude Opus 4.7 is Anthropic's most capable Opus model at its April 16, 2026 general-availability release, built for advanced, long-running software engineering and high-resolution image understanding. It is the first Claude model with high-resolution vision, accepting images up to about 3.75 megapixels versus roughly 1.15 megapixels on prior Claude models, and it adds a new 'xhigh' effort level between 'high' and 'max' for finer control over the reasoning-versus-latency trade-off. Anthropic ships it with safeguards that automatically detect and block high-risk cybersecurity requests, as part of a staged approach toward broader release of its more capable, access-restricted Mythos-class models.
advantages: Scores 87.6% on SWE-bench Verified, Anthropic's software-engineering benchmark (AWS Bedrock launch blog).
Scores 69.4% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, an agentic-coding benchmark (AWS Bedrock launch blog).
Scores 64.3% on SWE-bench Pro (AWS Bedrock launch blog).
First Claude model with high-resolution image support, accepting images Anthropic describes as more than three times larger than prior Claude versions could handle (Anthropic launch post).
disadvantages: Anthropic states it is less broadly capable than the access-restricted Claude Mythos Preview model (Anthropic launch post).
Anthropic states it is 'modestly weaker' than its predecessor on harm-reduction advice about controlled substances (Anthropic launch post).
Instruction-following changes mean prompts tuned for earlier Claude models can now produce unexpected results (Anthropic launch post).
Superseded within Anthropic's own Opus line by Opus 4.8, Opus 5 and Opus 5.5, all released within six months of Opus 4.7's launch (Anthropic model deprecations page).
use_cases: Advanced, long-running software engineering, including production-scale coding tasks
High-resolution visual analysis of charts, technical diagrams, and chemical structures
Finance and research agents for knowledge work such as financial analysis
Defensive cybersecurity work by users verified through the Cyber Verification Program

sources.title: Introducing Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.7 model in Amazon Bedrock

notes: Catalog facts (1M max input tokens, 128K max output tokens, deprecation_date 2027-04-16, anthropic/bedrock/vertex_ai-anthropic_models providers) match Anthropic's model-deprecations table entry for claude-opus-4-7 (Active, tentative retirement not sooner than April 16, 2027). Anthropic's own launch post presents most benchmark scores as chart images without text values, so SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0, and SWE-bench Pro are sourced to AWS's Bedrock launch blog, which republishes Anthropic's figures. The 90.9% BigLaw Bench figure on Anthropic's post is Harvey's own customer-testimonial score, not an Anthropic- or leaderboard-reported benchmark, so it was dropped from advantages and evaluations. The vision docs page's high-resolution/standard visual-token limits (4784 and 1568 tokens, 784 px^2/token) work out to about 3.75 and 1.23 megapixels, supporting the description's 'more than three times' comparison. The system-card PDF exceeded the size this tool can fetch.
